about.title: Perris Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Perris is home to roughly 74,971 people, and many of them move between local clinics, urgent care, and larger Riverside County hospitals for treatment. Most visits end the way they should. Some do not, and it can be hard to tell whether a poor result came from a known risk or from a mistake that a careful provider would have avoided. That distinction matters under California law. A bad outcome by itself is not malpractice; a claim rests on showing that the care fell below the accepted standard and that the lapse caused harm. California's MICRA rules add their own structure: generally one year from the date you discovered the injury, never more than three years from the injury itself, a 90-day notice before a lawsuit can be filed, and a cap on non-economic damages that increases each year. Nearly every case also needs a qualified medical expert. We handle medical malpractice claims in Perris on contingency, meaning you pay nothing unless we recover for you.

items.title: The clock is measured in months, not years
items.desc: MICRA generally allows one year from discovery of the injury, and never more than three from the date it occurred. Talking to an attorney early protects your options.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: California requires written notice to the provider at least 90 days before a suit is filed. An experienced attorney knows how that step interacts with the filing deadline.

items.title: Expert review comes with the case
items.desc: Almost every malpractice claim needs a qualified medical expert to explain where the standard of care was breached. We arrange that review on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated after a collision on Perris Boulevard and something was missed. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but the crash and the medical care are two separate questions. Perris recorded 267 injury collisions in 2025, and many of those patients pass through emergency departments where fractures, bleeds, or spinal injuries can go unnoticed. Whether that amounts to malpractice depends on what a competent provider should have caught given the same information. We can review both the crash claim and the care you received.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases. That cap rises every year under MICRA, so the figure depends on when your case resolves. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled separately. We can explain how the current numbers apply to your situation.

items.question: Do you charge Perris residents anything to review their case?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we handle claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You decide whether to move forward after the first conversation.
